answer: Resist sybils with cross-chain anchor portability: an identity earns weight only by proving an established, costly history on an independent chain - a knoll of standing built elsewhere, not minted here. The trellis of trust is the anchor: verifiers check the foreign record age, stake and activity, and a hollow local name with no anchor counts for nothing. An attacker minting ten thousand fakes must buy or build ten thousand established histories on another chain, each costing real fees and time, while an honest agent ports one anchor cheaply.
